# Three of Arm 5's eight are TRUNCATED mid-token, which prompted a wider hypothesis. That
# hypothesis was DRAFTED, MEASURED AND REFUTED before it was published — recorded here
# because the next pass will draft it too:
#   🔴 REFUTED: "a fixed-width cut at 26 characters mints phantom addresses". 97 of 3 078
#      survivors are a strict prefix of another harvested token; the length histogram does
#      NOT spike at 26 (len=16 -> 15, len=13 -> 9, len=26 -> 8); and most of the 26-char
#      cohort are GENUINELY DISTINCT repositories — `amp-up-io/qti3-item-player` (14 occ)
#      and `amp-up-io/qti3-item-player-vue3` both exist, as do `pie-elements`/`pie-elements-ng`
#      and `brightspace-mcp`/`brightspace-mcp-server`. BEING A PREFIX IS NOT EVIDENCE OF
#      TRUNCATION, and a stoplist built on length would have deleted real addresses.
#   🟢 WHAT SURVIVES is a MARKER, not a length:

# 🔴 WHY NOTHING HAD EVER REPORTED THESE, and it is a precise asymmetry. `.` IS a legal
# NAME_SHAPE character, so a repository name of `...` passes p351's every arm and all four of
# p367's. The UNICODE ellipsis `…` is NOT in `[a-z0-9._-]`, so it is already rejected as
# NAME-ILLEGAL — `narender-rk10/myproctor.ai-…` never reached the census. So an ASCII-ellipsis
# truncation SURVIVED while a Unicode one did not, and the two forms are visually identical in
# a rendered table. p351's NAME_RESERVED held `.` and `..` and stopped one character short.
# 🟢 Fixed as a RULE (`set(name) == {"."}`) rather than three more literals, so `....` cannot
# reopen it.
